name: Miradouro de Santa Luzia
seoTitle: Miradouro de Santa Luzia: Tiled Terrace 6 Minutes Uphill
tagline: Tiled terrace viewpoint over Alfama and the river, next door to Portas do Sol

description.short: Free terrace with azulejo panels and views over Alfama, 6 minutes uphill from the cruise terminal. When to go to avoid tour groups.
description.full:
Santa Luzia is the nearest of Lisbon's big viewpoints to the cruise terminal: about 400 m and 6 minutes on foot, but uphill through Alfama's lanes and stairs. Tram 28E and 12E stop outside at Miradouro Santa Luzia if you would rather ride. Miradouro das Portas do Sol is a minute or two further along the same street, so treat the two as one stop.

The terrace looks over Alfama's rooftops to the Tagus, with the dome of the Panteão Nacional and the towers of São Vicente de Fora on the skyline. Unlike Portas do Sol, much of the interest here is on the terrace itself: a pergola covered in bougainvillea, benches, and tiled panels on the wall of the Igreja de Santa Luzia.

If you have ten minutes, look first at the two azulejo panels on the church's south wall. One shows Terreiro do Paço, today's Praça do Comércio, with the royal palace that stood there before the 1755 earthquake; the other shows the Christian conquest of Lisbon in 1147. Then take the steps down to the lower terrace under the pergola for a second angle on the view, away from the street.

Between about 10:00 and 15:00 on busy ship days, tour groups and tuk-tuk drivers gather at the entrance and Tram 28E arrives packed. Earlier in the morning is calmer.

The viewpoint is free and never closes. Tuk-tuk drivers here offer rides to the castle and around the city; agree the price and route before getting in. The castle itself is about five minutes' walk uphill. What to skip: the souvenir stalls, which sell much the same as the rest of Alfama, and waiting for a tram back down when the walk to the ship takes minutes.
description.history: The viewpoint takes its name from the small Igreja de Santa Luzia e São Brás, a church of medieval origin associated with the Order of Malta that, like most of Lisbon, was damaged in 1755 and rebuilt. The two tile panels on its south wall are the reason to linger. The Terreiro do Paço panel is one of the few images of the riverside square as it looked before the earthquake, with the Ribeira Palace that Manuel I built when the court left the castle. The conquest panel recalls the siege of 1147, when Afonso Henriques and crusaders took the city; tradition says the knight Martim Moniz died holding open a castle gate, and the square where Tram 28E starts bears his name.
description.significance: Santa Luzia lets you compare Lisbon before and after 1755 at a glance: the tiled image of the vanished riverside palace on the wall, the rebuilt city and river in front of you. With Portas do Sol next door, it gives the quickest overview of Alfama for anyone short of time, with no ticket and no opening hours.

directions.general: Located in Alfama district just below São Jorge Castle, directly adjacent to (2 minutes from) Miradouro das Portas do Sol
directions.fromCruisePort: About 400 m and 6 minutes on foot, uphill through the lanes of Alfama; one of the closest viewpoints to the ship. Tram 28 stops outside.
directions.publicTransport: Tram 28E stops very close (Miradouro Santa Luzia stop). Tram 12E also accessible. From cruise port: walk to Santa Apolónia metro/train station, Blue Line to Terreiro do Paço, then Tram 28E uphill, or walk through Alfama from Sé Cathedral (steep 10-minute climb)
directions.parking: Extremely limited in Alfama - narrow medieval streets. Not recommended. Use tram or taxi

admissionPrices.notes: Free public viewpoint, open at all hours. Food and drink from nearby cafés are extra.

visitingInformation.bestTimeToVisit: Early morning (8:00-10:00 AM) for soft golden light and peaceful atmosphere before crowds. Late afternoon (4:00-6:00 PM) for beautiful light and comfortable temperature. Sunrise for magical light and solitude. Avoid midday heat in summer. Less crowded than Portas do Sol despite being next door
busyPeriods: Mid-morning to early afternoon (10:00 AM-2:00 PM)
After group tours from Portas do Sol
visitingInformation.adviceForVisitors: Visit both Santa Luzia and Portas do Sol viewpoints (2 minutes apart) - each offers unique perspectives. Take time to read the historic azulejo panels showing pre-1755 earthquake Lisbon - fascinating historical documentation. The lower terrace with circular iron windows offers unique photo framing opportunities. Bougainvillea is most vibrant in spring and summer. Combine with visit to nearby Santa Luzia church (when open). Street musicians often perform Fado - atmosphere is magical. Explore the 'lover's seats' (bancos dos namorados) - unique tiled benches where two seats face each other for romantic conversations. The viewpoint has two levels connected by stairs - explore both for different perspectives. Small market vendors nearby sell cork products and textiles at reasonable prices. Watch for pickpockets in crowded times

cruisePassengerInfo.timeNeededFromPort: About 1 hour including the walk up and back; 1.5 hours if you add Portas do Sol and a slower walk down through Alfama
cruisePassengerInfo.accessibility: Uphill 6-minute walk on stairs and cobbles from the terminal. The upper terrace is at street level by the tram stop; the lower terrace is reached by steps.
combinableWith: Miradouro das Portas do Sol (2-minute walk)
São Jorge Castle (8-10 minute walk uphill)
tips: Tram 28E and 12E stop at Miradouro Santa Luzia, by the terrace entrance; the on-board fare is €3.30 (Carris 2026).
See Portas do Sol at the same time: it is a minute or two along the same street.
The two historic azulejo panels are on the south wall of the Igreja de Santa Luzia: Terreiro do Paço before 1755, and the 1147 conquest of Lisbon.
Take the steps down to the lower terrace under the pergola for a different angle, away from the street.
Come before 10:00 or after 15:00 to avoid the peak of ship excursions and packed trams.
For the castle, the castle's own suggested route from this tram stop goes via Travessa de Santa Luzia and Largo do Contador-Mor, about five minutes uphill.
Tuk-tuk drivers wait at the entrance; agree the price and route before you get in.
Keep bags closed: the railing and Tram 28E are known pickpocket spots.

highlights: Two historic azulejo panels: Terreiro do Paço before 1755 and the 1147 conquest of Lisbon
View over Alfama's rooftops to the Tagus
Panteão Nacional dome and São Vicente de Fora on the skyline
Lower terrace under the pergola, reached by steps
Tram 28E and 12E stop at the entrance
Miradouro das Portas do Sol a minute or two away
facilities: Stairs connecting upper and lower terraces

accessibility.mobilityNotes: Limited wheelchair accessibility due to stairs between terrace levels and steep approaches through Alfama. Main upper terrace is relatively flat once reached via Tram 28E, but lower terrace requires descending stairs. Uneven cobblestone surfaces. Best access for mobility-limited visitors is via taxi/Uber to nearest accessible point, but stairs remain obstacle between levels. Upper terrace only is partially accessible
accessibility.visualAidServices: Azulejo panels have raised relief elements. Clear panoramic views
accessibility.hearingAidServices: Primarily visual experience - historic tile panels and views
